_note: D3A instrument binding for the 16 frozen TERMINAL identities. Each row quotes an exact substring of a supplied, byte-pinned document. This file is a locator table, not a scientific definition; a deciding author must supply the operative F/N/PRE-V3/SEAM/SOROK semantics at decision time.

F1.anchor: frozen TERMINAL F1 — descriptive first consumer
F1.exact_excerpt: current F1–F4 and missing recursive/minority/joint/directional functions
F1.consumer: F1–F4 first-use analytic family and its qualified recipient
F1.negative: a marginal-only or pairwise-substituted product must be refused as F1 evidence
F1.effect: preserve the descriptive family identity as a distinct first consumer
F1.why: first-use family is named in the common-frame mission and must not be dissolved into an undifferentiated query surface

F2.consumer: directional conditional recipient with its own denominator
F2.negative: using one direction's denominator for the reverse conditional must refuse
F2.effect: preserve direction and denominator as explicit contract fields
F2.why: reverse conditionals are not the transpose of a single joint table

F3.negative: unobserved or routed minority must not be reported as impossible
F3.effect: retain minority support and routing negatives as typed outputs
F3.why: mode-only reporting erases the configurations the downstream field actually needs

F4.anchor: frozen TERMINAL F4 — true same-person k>=3 joint
F4.negative: a synthetic product of pairwise marginals must be refused as F4
F4.effect: preserve respondent-coherent event identity for genuine high-order joints
F4.why: pairwise products cannot reconstitute three-way respondent patterns

F5.exact_excerpt: Old V552 contradiction tensor is empty; it is not an F5 implementation.
F5.consumer: historical F5 hypothesis owner; no current first reader
F5.negative: an empty historical tensor must not be presented as a live F5 engine
F5.effect: preserve F5 as historical capital, not an automatic current build
F5.why: historical absence of a tensor is not evidence of a missing current function

F6.anchor: frozen TERMINAL F6 — numeric uncovered mass versus permission guards
F6.exact_excerpt: F6 numeric uncovered mass versus permission guards
F6.consumer: F6 numeric estimand recipient with separate permission guard
F6.negative: a permission guard must not be silently replaced by a numeric estimate
F6.effect: keep numeric uncovered mass and rights guards as distinct outputs
F6.why: mixing a numeric estimand with a rights guard hides a real negative

F7.anchor: frozen TERMINAL F7 — measured comparability versus extrapolated time
F7.exact_excerpt: F7 observed comparability versus extrapolated time
F7.negative: extrapolated time must not be reported as observed comparability
F7.effect: preserve the observed/extrapolated distinction in the contract
F7.why: wave and instrument differences bound what comparison is measured

F8.anchor: frozen TERMINAL F8 — negative source selection
F8.negative: a negative source selection must not be rewritten as a positive observation
F8.effect: retain negative source selection as a first-class selectable outcome
F8.why: historical negative evidence is a conservation constraint, not an absence to be filled

N9.anchor: frozen TERMINAL N9 — direct material/objective case
N9.negative: a survey opinion must not be promoted to institutional power within N9
N9.effect: preserve a direct structural route that does not pass through survey marginals
N9.why: material relations may originate independently of survey respondents

N10E.anchor: frozen TERMINAL N10E — direct empirical possibility
N10E.negative: an absent material relation must not force a detour through N10W
N10E.effect: keep the direct empirical branch available without a universal world chain
N10E.why: direct branches may lawfully bypass unused intermediate products

N10W.anchor: frozen TERMINAL N10W — conditioned world possibility
N10W.negative: a joined hash alone must not count as a changed world opportunity
N10W.effect: require an actual conditioned option change, not only metadata identity
N10W.why: the selected world route must demonstrably condition an empirical candidate

N11.exact_excerpt: independent actors, exogenous world history, eventual SOROK continuation
N11.negative: a survey respondent must not become a fictional character
N11.effect: preserve a separately owned fictional world ingress
N11.why: world construction is a different authority class from observed evidence

N12.negative: world state must not automatically create actor knowledge
N12.effect: preserve actor access as a separate gated step
N12.why: access, comprehension and identification are not one operation

PRE-V3.anchor: frozen TERMINAL PRE-V3 — objective-world construction boundary
PRE-V3.exact_excerpt: Anticipate what **must** come into existence, including what does not yet exist
PRE-V3.negative: an unissued theoretical algorithm must not become a mandatory current build
PRE-V3.effect: type each PRE-V3 demand as build/conserve/allow/owner-held
PRE-V3.why: the architecture must not preclude plausible necessary future transformations

SEAM.anchor: frozen TERMINAL SEAM — joint boundary court
SEAM.negative: one programme must not issue the other's science
SEAM.effect: keep a bidirectional, asymmetrically owned boundary
SEAM.why: qualified output must meet an actually different programme's real first consumer

SOROK.anchor: frozen TERMINAL SOROK — independent developing actor
SOROK.negative: survey answers must not cause mandatory private motives
SOROK.effect: preserve actor psychology as a separate owner-held science
SOROK.why: C11 does not own actor psychology
